title: Découvrons l'art des fêtes
oneGoal: Students will recognize that art is used to celebrate special times

opening.activity: Show holiday art images from different cultures. Use gestures to show 'celebration' (clapping, dancing). Say 'C'est l'art!' while pointing to decorative items. Connect to students' experiences: 'Avez-vous vu l'art pour les fêtes?'
opening.visualSupports: Photo cards of holiday decorations, festive art from various traditions
opening.tpr: Clapping for celebration, pointing to art, dancing motions

mainActivity.activity: Gallery walk around classroom with holiday art examples. Students draw one thing they see that celebrates. Practice saying 'fête', 'art', 'célébrer' with actions. Create a class list of where we see celebration art.
mainActivity.visualSupports: Picture cards, gesture cards for vocabulary, drawing templates if needed
mainActivity.tpr: Point to art, draw in air, celebration gestures
mainActivity.differentiation: Provide drawing templates for struggling students, encourage detailed work for advanced students

closing.activity: Share one drawing with a partner. Practice saying 'C'est l'art pour célébrer.' Clean up materials together.
closing.visualSupports: Sentence strip with French phrase, cleanup picture schedule

decisionPoints.decision: How are students feeling about French today?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If overwhelmed: Use more English/gestures. If engaged: Add more French vocabulary.

decisionPoints.decision: What holiday experiences can they share?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If limited experience: Show more examples. If rich experience: Let them share and teach others.

decisionPoints.decision: Do they need more visual examples?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If confused about concept: Show more diverse art examples. If understanding: Move to creation faster.

emergencyBackup: If materials missing: Use classroom decorations as examples. If too complex: Just look at and name holiday colors in room.
realWorldConnection: Students see art in decorations at home and in community
progression: Foundation lesson - introduces the concept that art helps us celebrate

title: Les couleurs de l'hiver
oneGoal: Students will identify winter colors in holiday art

opening.activity: Review Lesson 1: 'Hier, nous avons vu l'art des fêtes.' Show winter scene photos. Point to colors and say 'couleur'. Demonstrate winter colors with paint swatches.
opening.visualSupports: Color cards, winter photographs, paint swatches
opening.tpr: Point to colors, shiver for 'hiver', show white with hands

mainActivity.activity: Color hunt around room for winter colors. Sort color cards into 'hiver' and 'pas hiver' groups. Paint or color with winter palette. Create simple winter color collage.
mainActivity.visualSupports: Color sorting mats, winter vs summer color comparison charts
mainActivity.tpr: Hold up colors, point around room, sorting motions
mainActivity.differentiation: Pre-cut shapes for fine motor struggles, extended color mixing for advanced students

closing.activity: Show collages to class. Practice 'Voici les couleurs d'hiver.' Vote on favorite winter color as class.
closing.visualSupports: Sentence strips, color voting board

decisionPoints.decision: Are students connecting colors to seasons?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If not connecting: Use more seasonal examples. If connecting well: Add subtle color variations.

decisionPoints.decision: Do they need more French color practice?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If struggling: Focus on 2-3 colors only. If confident: Add more color vocabulary.

decisionPoints.decision: What winter colors do they observe?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If limited observation: Guide attention to details. If good observation: Encourage artistic interpretation.

emergencyBackup: If art supplies unavailable: Use crayons to circle winter colors in magazines. If time short: Just sort pre-made color cards.
realWorldConnection: Winter colors appear in nature and holiday decorations around them
progression: Builds on Lesson 1 by connecting art to specific winter season

title: Mes traditions familiales
oneGoal: Students will share their family traditions through simple drawings

opening.activity: Connect to Lesson 2: 'Nous avons vu les couleurs d'hiver.' Show family celebration photos (diverse traditions). Use gesture for 'famille' (group hug motion). Say 'Chaque famille a des traditions.'
opening.visualSupports: Diverse family celebration photos, gesture cards
opening.tpr: Hug motion for famille, drawing motion in air, celebration gestures

mainActivity.activity: Students draw their family's way of celebrating (any tradition). Walk around, ask 'Qu'est-ce que c'est?' Practice vocabulary while drawing. Share with table partners.
mainActivity.visualSupports: Tradition example cards, vocabulary picture cards, drawing step guides
mainActivity.tpr: Drawing motions, family gestures, celebration movements
mainActivity.differentiation: Provide drawing templates, allow verbal sharing for non-drawers, celebrate all family structures

closing.activity: Gallery walk of family tradition drawings. Practice 'Ma famille...' sentence starter. Appreciate diversity with 'C'est beau!'
closing.visualSupports: Sentence starter cards, appreciation phrase cards

decisionPoints.decision: How comfortable are students sharing family traditions?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If hesitant: Start with your own example. If eager: Encourage detailed sharing.

decisionPoints.decision: Do they need vocabulary support?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If struggling with words: Use more visuals and gestures. If vocabulary strong: Add descriptive words.

decisionPoints.decision: Are all traditions being respected equally?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If some traditions overlooked: Highlight diversity explicitly. If all included: Celebrate the variety.

emergencyBackup: If drawing too complex: Just talk about traditions with picture cards. If sensitive family situations: Focus on classroom traditions instead.
realWorldConnection: Every family has special ways to celebrate that can be shown through art
progression: Builds on Lesson 2 by connecting personal experiences to art-making

title: Créons ensemble
oneGoal: Students will work together to create a class winter art piece

opening.activity: Review Lesson 3: 'Hier, vous avez dessiné vos traditions.' Demonstrate 'ensemble' by bringing hands together. Show large blank paper: 'Nous allons créer ensemble!'
opening.visualSupports: Hand gesture cards, large collaborative space setup
opening.tpr: Hands coming together, creating motions, group pointing

mainActivity.activity: Class collaborates on large winter scene. Each student adds one element. Practice turn-taking and French phrases: 'À mon tour', 'Très beau', 'Ensemble c'est mieux.'
mainActivity.visualSupports: Turn-taking cards, collaborative work examples, phrase strips
mainActivity.tpr: Taking turns gestures, adding motions, appreciation clapping
mainActivity.differentiation: Assign different complexity tasks, pair struggling students with helpers, celebrate all contributions

closing.activity: Step back and admire class creation. Practice 'Nous avons créé ensemble!' Take a class photo with the art.
closing.visualSupports: Achievement celebration cards, photo props

decisionPoints.decision: Are students ready for collaborative work?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If struggling to share: Model turn-taking explicitly. If collaborating well: Add more complex group decisions.

decisionPoints.decision: What materials work best for group projects?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If materials causing conflict: Provide duplicates. If working well: Add variety for creativity.

decisionPoints.decision: How can everyone contribute meaningfully?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If some excluded: Assign specific roles. If all involved: Let natural collaboration continue.

emergencyBackup: If collaboration too difficult: Work in pairs instead of whole class. If materials insufficient: Use drawing on shared paper.
realWorldConnection: Communities work together to create beautiful holiday displays
progression: Builds on Lesson 3 by moving from individual to collaborative art-making

title: Formes de l'hiver
oneGoal: Students will create winter shapes using basic geometric forms

opening.activity: Connect to Lesson 4: 'Hier, nous avons créé ensemble.' Show winter objects (snowflake, tree, ornament). Trace shapes in air: 'Voici un rond, un triangle.' Use body to make shapes.
opening.visualSupports: Large shape cards, winter object photos, shape tracing guides
opening.tpr: Trace shapes in air, make body shapes, point to shapes in objects

mainActivity.activity: Shape hunt in winter pictures. Students trace and cut basic shapes. Combine shapes to make winter objects (triangle trees, round snowmen). Practice shape names while creating.
mainActivity.visualSupports: Shape sorting mats, winter object assembly guides, vocabulary cards
mainActivity.tpr: Tracing motions, cutting motions, combining gestures
mainActivity.differentiation: Pre-cut shapes for fine motor needs, complex shape combinations for advanced students

closing.activity: Shape show-and-tell: 'J'ai fait un... avec des...' Display creations on shape sorting board.
closing.visualSupports: Sentence starter cards, shape display board

decisionPoints.decision: Are students recognizing shapes in winter objects?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If not seeing shapes: Point out more explicitly with tracing. If recognizing well: Challenge with complex objects.

decisionPoints.decision: Do they need more practice with shape vocabulary?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If struggling with names: Focus on 2 shapes only. If confident: Add more shape words.

decisionPoints.decision: What tools help them create clean shapes?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If cutting difficult: Provide templates and guidance. If cutting well: Encourage freehand shapes.

emergencyBackup: If scissors unavailable: Tear shapes from paper or use pre-cut shapes. If too complex: Just identify shapes in pictures.
realWorldConnection: Winter symbols like snowflakes, trees, and ornaments all use basic shapes
progression: Builds on Lesson 4 by introducing specific artistic elements (shape)

title: Décorations simples
oneGoal: Students will make simple decorations using paper and basic materials

opening.activity: Review Lesson 5: 'Hier, nous avons fait des formes.' Show simple paper decorations. Demonstrate 'décoration' by hanging one up. Practice scissor safety: 'Attention avec les ciseaux!'
opening.visualSupports: Decoration examples, safety poster for scissors, step-by-step photos
opening.tpr: Hanging motions, cutting motions, safety gestures

mainActivity.activity: Students make paper chain decorations or simple snowflakes. Focus on safe scissor use and following steps. Practice vocabulary while creating: 'Je coupe le papier.'
mainActivity.visualSupports: Step-by-step instruction cards, safety reminders, finished examples
mainActivity.tpr: Cutting motions, folding motions, decorating gestures
mainActivity.differentiation: Pre-cut strips for fine motor support, more intricate patterns for advanced students

closing.activity: Hang decorations around classroom. Practice 'Voici ma décoration!' Admire everyone's work with 'C'est joli!'
closing.visualSupports: Appreciation phrase cards, decoration display area

decisionPoints.decision: Are students safe with scissors?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If unsafe practices: Review safety rules immediately. If using safely: Allow more independence.

decisionPoints.decision: Do they need help with cutting techniques?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If struggling with cutting: Provide hand-over-hand guidance. If cutting well: Introduce curved cuts.

decisionPoints.decision: What level of independence can they handle?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If needing constant help: Simplify steps further. If working independently: Add creative choices.

emergencyBackup: If scissors concerns arise: Use tear-decorations or pre-cut pieces. If time short: Make simple paper chains only.
realWorldConnection: Families make decorations together to beautify their homes
progression: Builds on Lesson 5 by applying shapes to create functional art (decorations)

title: Cartes de souhaits
oneGoal: Students will create greeting cards with winter symbols

opening.activity: Connect to Lesson 6: 'Hier, nous avons fait des décorations.' Show greeting cards from different cultures. Open and close cards: 'C'est une carte!' Point to winter symbols: 'Voici des symboles.'
opening.visualSupports: Various greeting cards, winter symbol chart, gesture cards
opening.tpr: Opening/closing motions, pointing to symbols, drawing motions

mainActivity.activity: Students create greeting cards with winter symbols. Add simple French messages like 'Bonne fête!' or draw pictures to communicate. Practice vocabulary while decorating.
mainActivity.visualSupports: French greeting examples, symbol reference sheet, card folding guide
mainActivity.tpr: Drawing motions, card opening gestures, message writing motions
mainActivity.differentiation: Pre-written messages for non-writers, blank cards for creative writers, symbol stamps for fine motor support

closing.activity: Share cards with partners. Practice 'Voici ma carte!' Discuss who they might give cards to: 'Pour ma famille!'
closing.visualSupports: Sharing sentence strips, family vocabulary cards

decisionPoints.decision: Can students write simple French greetings?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If not writing yet: Focus on symbols and copying. If writing: Encourage original messages.

decisionPoints.decision: What symbols are meaningful to each child?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If limited symbol knowledge: Provide reference sheet. If rich understanding: Encourage personal symbol choices.

decisionPoints.decision: Do they need templates or can they design freely?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If overwhelmed by choices: Provide templates. If confident: Allow free design.

emergencyBackup: If card-making too complex: Decorate pre-made cards. If writing difficult: Focus only on pictures and symbols.
realWorldConnection: People send cards to share love and good wishes during celebrations
progression: Builds on Lesson 6 by combining decoration skills with communication purpose

title: Cadeaux faits main
oneGoal: Students will create simple handmade gifts

opening.activity: Review Lesson 7: 'Hier, nous avons fait des cartes.' Show handmade gifts. Use hands to demonstrate 'fait à la main.' Practice 'C'est un cadeau!' with giving gestures.
opening.visualSupports: Handmade gift examples, hand gesture cards, giving motion pictures
opening.tpr: Hand-making motions, giving gestures, wrapping motions

mainActivity.activity: Students create simple gifts (decorated containers, bookmarks, painted stones). Focus on the care in making something for someone else. Practice 'Je donne un cadeau.'
mainActivity.visualSupports: Gift-making step guides, caring gesture cards, finished examples
mainActivity.tpr: Creating motions, caring gestures, giving actions
mainActivity.differentiation: Simpler projects for fine motor needs, more detailed work for advanced students, focus on effort over perfection

closing.activity: Wrap gifts in simple materials. Practice 'C'est fait avec amour!' Discuss the joy of giving vs. receiving.
closing.visualSupports: Emotion cards, giving vs. receiving pictures

decisionPoints.decision: What gifts are appropriate for their skill level?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If skills limited: Choose very simple projects. If capable: Allow more complex creations.

decisionPoints.decision: Are they understanding the joy of giving?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If focused on receiving: Emphasize making others happy. If understanding giving: Celebrate their generosity.

decisionPoints.decision: Do they need help with wrapping or presentation?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If struggling with wrapping: Provide simple bags/boxes. If managing well: Add decorative elements.

emergencyBackup: If craft supplies limited: Decorate paper bags as gifts. If too complex: Make simple drawings as gifts.
realWorldConnection: Handmade gifts show extra care and thoughtfulness
progression: Builds on Lesson 7 by extending card-making into gift creation

title: Textures d'hiver
oneGoal: Students will explore different textures in winter-themed art

opening.activity: Connect to Lesson 8: 'Hier, nous avons fait des cadeaux.' Touch different materials: cotton (soft snow), sandpaper (rough bark). Practice 'doux' and 'rugueux' with facial expressions.
opening.visualSupports: Texture sample board, expression cards for soft/rough, winter texture photos
opening.tpr: Touching motions, soft/rough facial expressions, winter texture gestures

mainActivity.activity: Texture exploration station. Students feel materials and sort into 'doux' and 'rugueux.' Create winter collages using different textures to represent snow, trees, ice.
mainActivity.visualSupports: Texture sorting mats, winter scene examples, texture vocabulary cards
mainActivity.tpr: Feeling motions, sorting gestures, collage creation actions
mainActivity.differentiation: More texture options for sensory seekers, fewer overwhelming textures for sensitive students

closing.activity: Touch and describe textures: 'C'est doux comme...' 'C'est rugueux comme...' Display texture art gallery-style.
closing.visualSupports: Comparison sentence starters, texture description cards

decisionPoints.decision: Are students exploring textures safely?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If unsafe exploration: Supervise more closely. If exploring safely: Allow more independence.

decisionPoints.decision: What materials create interesting winter textures?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If limited material interest: Introduce new textures. If engaged with materials: Let them experiment freely.

decisionPoints.decision: Do they need vocabulary support for describing textures?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If struggling with descriptions: Provide more examples. If describing well: Add more texture words.

emergencyBackup: If texture materials unavailable: Use classroom objects for texture exploration. If sensory issues: Make texture exploration optional.
realWorldConnection: Winter brings different textures - soft snow, rough bark, smooth ice
progression: Builds on Lesson 8 by adding tactile elements to art-making

title: Lumières et ombres
oneGoal: Students will create art showing light and shadow effects

opening.activity: Review Lesson 9: 'Hier, nous avons touché les textures.' Darken room, use flashlight to create shadows. Point to light: 'C'est la lumière!' Point to shadow: 'C'est l'ombre!'
opening.visualSupports: Light/shadow demonstration setup, vocabulary cards with symbols
opening.tpr: Shining motions, shadow pointing, brightness gestures

mainActivity.activity: Shadow play with objects and flashlights. Students trace shadows on paper. Create 'light' pictures with bright colors and 'shadow' pictures with dark colors.
mainActivity.visualSupports: Shadow tracing guides, light/dark color examples, holiday light photos
mainActivity.tpr: Tracing motions, shining actions, light/dark comparisons
mainActivity.differentiation: Partner support for shadow tracing, independent exploration for confident students

closing.activity: Compare light and shadow artworks. Practice 'Voici la lumière, voici l'ombre.' Connect to holiday lights they've seen.
closing.visualSupports: Light/shadow comparison charts, holiday light examples

decisionPoints.decision: Do students understand light and shadow concepts?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If concepts unclear: Do more demonstration. If understanding: Let them experiment independently.

decisionPoints.decision: What tools help them create these effects?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If struggling with tools: Simplify to basic tracing. If using tools well: Add more complex shadow play.

decisionPoints.decision: Are they making connections to holiday lights?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If not connecting: Show more holiday light examples. If connecting: Discuss their experiences with lights.

emergencyBackup: If flashlights unavailable: Use window light for shadows. If too dark in room: Focus on bright/dark color concepts only.
realWorldConnection: Holiday celebrations often feature special lighting and candles
progression: Builds on Lesson 9 by adding another artistic element (light/shadow)

title: Motifs répétés
oneGoal: Students will create patterns using winter and holiday motifs

opening.activity: Connect to Lesson 10: 'Hier, nous avons vu la lumière et l'ombre.' Show patterned holiday decorations. Demonstrate 'répéter' by repeating actions. Point to patterns: 'Voici un motif!'
opening.visualSupports: Patterned decoration examples, repetition demonstration cards, motif identification sheets
opening.tpr: Repeating motions, pointing to patterns, stamping actions

mainActivity.activity: Pattern detective hunt in room. Students identify repeating motifs. Create their own patterns using winter stamps or drawings. Practice 'Je répète le motif.'
mainActivity.visualSupports: Pattern identification guides, winter motif reference sheets, pattern creation templates
mainActivity.tpr: Detective searching motions, stamping actions, pattern creation gestures
mainActivity.differentiation: Simple AB patterns for beginners, complex patterns for advanced students, pattern templates for support

closing.activity: Pattern show and tell. Students describe their patterns: 'Mon motif répète...' Create class pattern book.
closing.visualSupports: Pattern description sentence starters, class book template

decisionPoints.decision: Are students understanding pattern concepts?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If pattern concepts unclear: Use simpler AB patterns. If understanding: Introduce ABC patterns.

decisionPoints.decision: What motifs are they most drawn to?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If limited motif interest: Introduce more options. If strong preferences: Build on their interests.

decisionPoints.decision: Do they need help with spacing and repetition?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If spacing difficult: Provide templates with guides. If managing spacing: Allow freehand patterns.

emergencyBackup: If stamps unavailable: Use finger painting for patterns. If too complex: Just identify existing patterns in room.
realWorldConnection: Traditional holiday decorations often feature repeating patterns
progression: Builds on Lesson 10 by introducing pattern-making with familiar symbols

title: Mon chef-d'œuvre
oneGoal: Students will combine all learned techniques in a personal masterpiece
materials: Various art supplies from previous lessons

opening.activity: Review all previous lessons with visual reminders. Explain 'chef-d'œuvre' as 'your best art.' Show how artists 'combiner' different techniques. Let students choose their focus.
opening.visualSupports: Lesson review poster, technique choice board, masterpiece examples
opening.tpr: Combining motions, choice gestures, proud pointing

mainActivity.activity: Students create their masterpiece using any combination of learned techniques (shapes, colors, textures, patterns, etc.). Circulate and practice vocabulary: 'J'ai combiné...'
mainActivity.visualSupports: Technique reminder cards, planning templates, step-by-step guides
mainActivity.tpr: Creating motions, combining gestures, artistic actions
mainActivity.differentiation: Support planning for overwhelmed students, encourage complex combinations for advanced students

closing.activity: Students place masterpieces in portfolios. Practice 'C'est mon chef-d'œuvre!' Plan for sharing in next lesson.
closing.visualSupports: Portfolio labels, sharing preparation cards

decisionPoints.decision: What techniques do students want to showcase?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If unsure about choices: Provide technique menu. If clear preferences: Support their artistic vision.

decisionPoints.decision: Do they need help planning their composition?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If overwhelmed by planning: Provide simple templates. If planning well: Encourage detailed composition.

decisionPoints.decision: Are they ready for more independent work?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If needing support: Provide more guidance. If working independently: Step back and observe.

emergencyBackup: If choices overwhelming: Assign specific technique combinations. If time short: Focus on one favorite technique only.
realWorldConnection: Artists combine different skills to create meaningful works
progression: Builds on Lesson 11 by synthesizing all previous learning into one piece

title: Galerie de classe
oneGoal: Students will display and discuss their artwork like in a real gallery

opening.activity: Connect to Lesson 12: 'Hier, vous avez fini vos chef-d'œuvres!' Set up classroom like art gallery. Practice gallery manners: quiet walking, careful looking. Demonstrate 'montrer' and 'expliquer.'
opening.visualSupports: Gallery setup photos, gallery behavior cards, presentation gesture guides
opening.tpr: Quiet walking, careful looking motions, presentation gestures

mainActivity.activity: Gallery walk where students present their masterpieces. Practice 'Voici mon art. J'ai utilisé...' Other students practice appreciation: 'C'est beau!' 'J'aime...'
mainActivity.visualSupports: Presentation sentence starters, appreciation phrase cards, gallery viewing guides
mainActivity.tpr: Presentation motions, appreciation gestures, gallery walking
mainActivity.differentiation: Support nervous presenters with partners, encourage detailed explanations from confident students

closing.activity: Vote for favorite gallery experience (not artwork). Practice 'Notre galerie est magnifique!' Take photos for portfolios.
closing.visualSupports: Gallery reflection cards, photo permission and props

decisionPoints.decision: Are students ready to present their work?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If nervous about presenting: Pair with confident partners. If eager to present: Allow extended sharing time.

decisionPoints.decision: What vocabulary do they need for descriptions?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If lacking description words: Provide word banks. If vocabulary strong: Encourage detailed descriptions.

decisionPoints.decision: How can we make everyone feel proud of their art?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If some students seem less confident: Highlight unique aspects of each work. If all confident: Focus on artistic growth.

emergencyBackup: If gallery setup impossible: Do table-to-table sharing. If presentations too long: Limit to one technique per student.
realWorldConnection: Artists display their work for others to enjoy and appreciate
progression: Builds on Lesson 12 by celebrating and sharing completed artwork

title: Réflexion artistique
oneGoal: Students will reflect on their learning and artistic growth

opening.activity: Review journey from Lesson 1 to 13 using visual timeline. Practice 'réflexion' by thinking gesture. Show growth from first drawings to masterpieces: 'Vous avez grandi!'
opening.visualSupports: Learning journey timeline, growth comparison examples, thinking gesture cards
opening.tpr: Thinking gestures, growing motions, pointing to progress

mainActivity.activity: Students look through portfolios and identify learning. Complete simple reflection sheets with drawings/words. Practice 'J'ai appris...' 'Je peux maintenant...' Share growth with partners.
mainActivity.visualSupports: Reflection sheet templates, learning vocabulary cards, portfolio organization guides
mainActivity.tpr: Thinking motions, learning gestures, sharing actions
mainActivity.differentiation: Picture-based reflections for non-writers, detailed reflections for advanced students

closing.activity: Class celebration of artistic growth. Practice 'Nous sommes des artistes!' Plan how to share learning with families.
closing.visualSupports: Celebration materials, artist identity cards, family sharing planning sheets

decisionPoints.decision: Can students identify what they've learned?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If struggling to identify learning: Use portfolio prompts. If identifying well: Encourage detailed reflection.

decisionPoints.decision: Are they proud of their progress?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If not recognizing growth: Highlight specific improvements. If proud of progress: Celebrate their achievements.

decisionPoints.decision: What art goals do they have for the future?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If no future goals: Suggest possibilities based on interests. If clear goals: Support their artistic aspirations.

emergencyBackup: If reflection too abstract: Focus on favorite artworks only. If time limited: Do verbal reflection circle only.
realWorldConnection: Artists always reflect on their work to continue growing
progression: Builds on Lesson 13 by completing the learning cycle with self-assessment

title: Art collaboratif
oneGoal: Students will work together on a large collaborative winter mural

opening.activity: EXTENSION: Review collaborative work from Lesson 4. Show large mural space. Plan together what winter scene to create. Assign roles based on student strengths and interests.
opening.visualSupports: Mural planning sheets, role cards, collaborative work examples
opening.tpr: Planning gestures, role assignment motions, collaborative actions

mainActivity.activity: Students work in assigned roles to create mural sections. Practice collaborative vocabulary and problem-solving. Combine individual sections into cohesive whole.
mainActivity.visualSupports: Section planning guides, collaborative vocabulary reminders, problem-solving strategy cards
mainActivity.tpr: Creating motions, combining gestures, collaborative actions
mainActivity.differentiation: Assign roles matching student abilities, provide collaboration support as needed

closing.activity: Step back and admire collaborative mural. Celebrate teamwork and individual contributions. Display prominently in school.
closing.visualSupports: Teamwork celebration cards, display planning materials

decisionPoints.decision: How well are students collaborating?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If collaboration difficult: Provide more structure and mediation. If collaborating well: Allow more creative freedom.

decisionPoints.decision: What roles work best for each child?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If roles not matching: Adjust assignments. If roles working well: Let students develop expertise.

decisionPoints.decision: Are they building on each other's ideas?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If working in isolation: Encourage idea sharing. If building together: Celebrate creative collaboration.

emergencyBackup: If mural too ambitious: Create smaller collaborative pieces. If collaboration breaking down: Return to individual work within group project.
realWorldConnection: Community art projects bring people together
progression: Extension - applies all learned skills in collaborative format

title: Techniques avancées
oneGoal: Students will experiment with more advanced art techniques

opening.activity: EXTENSION: Show advanced techniques (watercolor blending, printmaking, mixed media). Let students choose which techniques to explore. Set up exploration stations.
opening.visualSupports: Technique demonstration cards, station setup guides, choice boards
opening.tpr: Demonstration motions, exploration gestures, choice actions

mainActivity.activity: Station rotation where students try advanced techniques. Focus on experimentation and discovery rather than perfection. Document techniques they enjoy most.
mainActivity.visualSupports: Station instruction cards, technique documentation sheets, discovery celebration materials
mainActivity.tpr: Exploration motions, discovery gestures, documentation actions
mainActivity.differentiation: Provide varying levels of challenge, support struggling students, celebrate all attempts

closing.activity: Share favorite new techniques discovered. Plan which ones to use in future projects. Celebrate willingness to try new things.
closing.visualSupports: Technique sharing cards, future planning sheets, risk-taking celebration materials

decisionPoints.decision: Which students are ready for new challenges?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If some not ready: Provide familiar techniques with small variations. If ready for challenge: Introduce more complex techniques.

decisionPoints.decision: What techniques interest them most?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If limited interest: Try different technique options. If strong interest: Allow deeper exploration.

decisionPoints.decision: Do they need additional support or materials?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If techniques too difficult: Simplify or provide more support. If managing well: Increase complexity.

emergencyBackup: If advanced supplies unavailable: Modify familiar techniques in new ways. If techniques too challenging: Focus on perfecting basic techniques.
realWorldConnection: Artists continually learn new ways to express themselves
progression: Extension - enriches previous learning with new techniques

title: Art numérique simple
oneGoal: Students will explore basic digital art tools for winter themes

opening.activity: EXTENSION: Show digital art examples alongside traditional art. Demonstrate simple digital tools. Connect to winter themes they've explored in previous lessons.
opening.visualSupports: Digital vs traditional art comparison, simple tool demonstration, winter theme examples
opening.tpr: Digital tool motions, comparison gestures, winter theme actions

mainActivity.activity: Students explore simple digital drawing tools to create winter scenes. Focus on how digital tools can create effects similar to traditional techniques. Save and share digital creations.
mainActivity.visualSupports: Digital tool guides, winter scene templates, sharing instruction cards
mainActivity.tpr: Digital creation motions, tool exploration gestures, sharing actions
mainActivity.differentiation: Partner support for technology challenges, independent exploration for tech-comfortable students

closing.activity: Compare digital and traditional winter artworks. Discuss benefits of each medium. Display digital art alongside traditional pieces.
closing.visualSupports: Medium comparison charts, display planning materials, reflection cards

decisionPoints.decision: Are students comfortable with digital tools?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If uncomfortable with technology: Provide more support and simpler tools. If comfortable: Allow more complex digital exploration.

decisionPoints.decision: What level of tech support do they need?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If needing constant support: Pair with tech-comfortable partners. If managing independently: Encourage creative experimentation.

decisionPoints.decision: How can we balance digital and traditional art?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If preferring one medium: Encourage trying both. If using both well: Let them combine digital and traditional techniques.

emergencyBackup: If technology issues: Use traditional tools to create 'digital-style' effects. If apps too complex: Use simpler drawing programs.
realWorldConnection: Modern artists use both traditional and digital tools
progression: Extension - introduces technology while reinforcing winter art themes

title: Art recyclé
oneGoal: Students will create winter art using recycled materials

opening.activity: EXTENSION: Show recycled art examples. Discuss how artists can help environment by reusing materials. Sort available recycled materials by type and potential use.
opening.visualSupports: Recycled art examples, environmental care books, material sorting guides
opening.tpr: Sorting motions, environmental care gestures, creative reuse actions

mainActivity.activity: Students create winter sculptures or collages using recycled materials. Focus on creative problem-solving and seeing new possibilities in discarded items.
mainActivity.visualSupports: Creative reuse idea cards, winter theme guides, problem-solving strategy reminders
mainActivity.tpr: Creative building motions, problem-solving gestures, reuse actions
mainActivity.differentiation: Pre-sorted materials for overwhelmed students, complex construction challenges for advanced students

closing.activity: Recycled art showcase. Discuss how art can help care for our planet. Plan classroom recycling art collection.
closing.visualSupports: Environmental care celebration materials, recycling collection planning sheets

decisionPoints.decision: What recycled materials are safe and available?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If limited safe materials: Use classroom recyclables only. If good material variety: Allow more complex construction.

decisionPoints.decision: Are students understanding environmental connections?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If not connecting to environment: Provide more environmental education. If understanding: Encourage environmental action planning.

decisionPoints.decision: How creative can they be with unconventional materials?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If struggling with creativity: Provide idea prompts. If very creative: Celebrate innovative solutions.

emergencyBackup: If recycled materials unavailable: Use classroom paper scraps for collage. If safety concerns: Pre-sort materials more carefully.
realWorldConnection: Artists can create beauty while caring for our planet
progression: Extension - applies art skills while introducing environmental awareness

title: Performance artistique
oneGoal: Students will combine visual art with movement and music

opening.activity: EXTENSION: Show how art can be combined with music and movement. Demonstrate creating art while music plays. Practice winter movements (falling snow, growing trees).
opening.visualSupports: Multi-art examples, movement demonstration cards, winter movement guides
opening.tpr: Multi-art creation motions, winter movements, musical gestures

mainActivity.activity: Students create art while winter music plays, incorporating movement into creation process. Paint to music rhythms, dance while creating, use art tools as musical instruments.
mainActivity.visualSupports: Movement-art integration guides, rhythm visual aids, creative expression examples
mainActivity.tpr: Rhythmic creation motions, dance movements, expressive gestures
mainActivity.differentiation: Quiet movement options for sensitive students, dynamic movement for kinesthetic learners

closing.activity: Performance showcase where students present art with movement or music. Celebrate creative expression and multi-art connections.
closing.visualSupports: Performance celebration materials, multi-art appreciation cards

decisionPoints.decision: Are students comfortable with performance elements?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If uncomfortable performing: Make performances optional. If enjoying performance: Encourage creative expression.

decisionPoints.decision: How can visual art enhance their movement?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If not seeing connections: Demonstrate art-movement links. If making connections: Support their creative combinations.

decisionPoints.decision: What music supports their winter themes?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If music not inspiring: Try different winter music styles. If music working well: Let students choose music for creation.

emergencyBackup: If performance too overwhelming: Focus on creating art while listening to music. If space limited: Do individual art-music connections at desks.
realWorldConnection: Many celebrations combine different art forms together
progression: Extension - expands art beyond visual into multisensory experience

title: Célébration finale
oneGoal: Students will share their complete winter art journey with families

opening.activity: EXTENSION: Prepare for family celebration. Organize portfolios and select pieces to display. Practice sharing their learning journey with simple French phrases.
opening.visualSupports: Portfolio organization guides, presentation phrase cards, celebration planning materials
opening.tpr: Organization motions, presentation practice gestures, celebration preparations

mainActivity.activity: Family celebration event. Students present portfolios, demonstrate techniques, and share favorite artworks. Families participate in simple art activity together.
mainActivity.visualSupports: Presentation guides, family activity instructions, celebration setup materials
mainActivity.tpr: Presentation gestures, demonstration motions, family interaction actions
mainActivity.differentiation: Support nervous presenters, celebrate all participation levels, accommodate family circumstances

closing.activity: Celebration reflection. Students share favorite moments from art journey. Plan continued art exploration. Thank families for support.
closing.visualSupports: Journey reflection materials, future planning cards, gratitude expression guides

decisionPoints.decision: How can we showcase everyone's growth?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If some students less confident: Highlight individual strengths. If all confident: Focus on collective achievements.

decisionPoints.decision: What presentation format works best?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If formal presentations challenging: Use informal sharing circles. If students ready: Support more structured presentations.

decisionPoints.decision: Are families able to attend and celebrate?
decisionPoints.ifThen: If families cannot attend: Create video presentations to share. If good attendance: Make celebration interactive.

emergencyBackup: If family event not possible: Celebrate with other classes or school community. If time limited: Focus on student reflection and pride in achievements.
realWorldConnection: Art brings families and communities together in celebration
progression: Extension - culminates all learning in celebration with community
